The **Narval-class submarines** were a series of diesel-electric attack submarines built for the **French Navy (Marine Nationale)** in the late 1950s and early 1960s. They were among the first post-WWII submarines designed in France and represented a significant step in the country's submarine development. Here’s a detailed overview: --- ### **1. Background & Development** - **Purpose**: The Narval-class was designed as **long-range, ocean-going attack submarines** to replace older WWII-era submarines (such as the *Saphir*-class) and counter Soviet naval threats during the Cold War. - **Design Influence**: The class was influenced by German Type XXI U-boats (captured after WWII) and incorporated lessons from French wartime submarine operations. - **Builder**: **Cherbourg Naval Dockyard (DCN, now Naval Group)**. - **Construction Period**: 1951–1960 (commissioned between 1957 and 1960). --- ### **2. Technical Specifications** | **Parameter** | **Details** | |-----------------------------|------------| | **Displacement** | 1,320 tons (surfaced), 1,635 tons (submerged) | | **Length** | 78.4 meters (257 ft) | | **Beam** | 7.8 meters (26 ft) | | **Draft** | 5.2 meters (17 ft) | | **Propulsion** | - 2 × diesel engines (2,400 hp total)
- 2 × electric motors (2,600 hp total)
- 2 × shafts | | **Speed** | 16 knots (surfaced), 18 knots (submerged) | | **Range** | 15,000 nautical miles (28,000 km) at 8 knots (surfaced)
100 nautical miles (190 km) at 5 knots (submerged) | | **Test Depth** | 200 meters (656 ft) | | **Crew** | 63 (7 officers, 56 enlisted) | | **Endurance** | 30 days | --- ### **3. Armament** - **Torpedoes**: - 8 × 550 mm (21.7 in) torpedo tubes (6 bow, 2 stern). - Carried **14 torpedoes** (typically **L3 or L5 anti-submarine torpedoes** or **F17 anti-ship torpedoes**). - **Mines**: - Could lay **32 mines** in place of torpedoes. - **Guns** (early service): - 1 × 100 mm (3.9 in) deck gun (removed in later refits). --- ### **4. Sensors & Electronics** - **Radar**: DRUA 31 surface search radar. - **Sonar**: - DUUA 1 passive sonar. - DUUX 2 active/passive sonar (later models). - **Fire Control**: Early analog systems (upgraded in later refits). --- ### **5. Operational History** - **Cold War Role**: Primarily used for **anti-submarine warfare (ASW)**, **patrol missions**, and **intelligence gathering** in the Atlantic and Mediterranean. - **Deployments**: - Participated in NATO exercises. - Conducted surveillance missions near Soviet naval bases. - **Incidents**: - **1968**: *Dauphin* (S633) collided with a Soviet submarine in the Mediterranean (details classified). - **1970s**: Several boats were involved in tracking Soviet ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs). - **Modernization**: - **1970s**: Some boats received **new sonar (DUUA 2A)** and **torpedo upgrades**. - **1980s**: *Narval* (S631) and *Marsouin* (S632) were fitted with **SM39 Exocet anti-ship missiles** (a rare modification for diesel subs). --- ### **6. Boats of the Class** Six submarines were built: | **Name** | **Pennant** | **Commissioned** | **Decommissioned** | **Fate** | |----------------|------------|------------------|--------------------|----------| | *Narval* | S631 | 1957 | 1986 | Scrapped | | *Marsouin* | S632 | 1957 | 1982 | Scrapped | | *Dauphin* | S633 | 1958 | 1992 | Scrapped | | *Requin* | S634 | 1958 | 1985 | Scrapped | | *Espadon* | S637 | 1960 | 1985 | Museum ship (Saint-Nazaire) | | *Morse* | S638 | 1960 | 1986 | Scrapped | - **Preserved Boat**: *Espadon* (S637) is now a **museum submarine** in **Saint-Nazaire, France**, open to the public. --- ### **7. Successor & Legacy** - **Replacement**: The Narval-class was succeeded by the **Agosta-class** (1970s) and later the **Rubis-class** (nuclear attack submarines). - **Influence**: The class provided valuable experience for French submarine design, leading to more advanced boats like the **Daphné-class** (1960s) and **Agosta-class**. - **Notable Features**: - One of the first French submarines with a **teardrop hull** (for better hydrodynamics). - Early adoption of **diesel-electric propulsion** with snorkel capability. --- ### **8. Comparison with Contemporaries** | **Class** | **Country** | **Displacement (submerged)** | **Speed (submerged)** | **Torpedo Tubes** | |-----------------|------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------|-------------------| | **Narval** | France | 1,635 tons | 18 knots | 8 (6 bow, 2 stern)| | **Type XXI** | Germany | 1,819 tons | 17 knots | 6 (bow) | | **Tang-class** | USA | 2,700 tons | 16 knots | 6 (bow) | | **Whiskey-class** | USSR | 1,350 tons | 13 knots | 6 (bow) | The Narval-class was **faster and more heavily armed** than many contemporaries but lacked the endurance of nuclear submarines. --- ### **9. Why Were They Retired?** - **Aging Technology**: By the 1980s, their **sonar and fire control systems** were outdated. - **Nuclear Shift**: France prioritized **nuclear-powered submarines (Rubis-class)** for long-range missions. - **Cost of Upgrades**: Modernizing diesel-electric subs was less cost-effective than building new nuclear boats. --- ### **10. Interesting Facts** - **First French Post-War Submarines**: The Narval-class marked France’s return to submarine construction after WWII. - **Espadon’s Museum Role**: *Espadon* is one of the few preserved Cold War-era submarines in Europe. - **Exocet Missile Test**: *Narval* was one of the first diesel submarines to test the **SM39 Exocet** (a capability later used in the *Agosta*-class). - **Silent Running**: Designed for **low noise levels**, making them effective in ASW roles. --- ### **Conclusion** The **Narval-class** was a crucial step in France’s post-war submarine fleet, bridging the gap between WWII-era boats and modern nuclear submarines. While overshadowed by later classes, they played a key role in Cold War naval operations and helped shape French submarine design. Would you like details on any specific boat or operational mission?
